note: RFC 6286 Section 2.1 says: The BGP Identifier is a 4-octet, unsigned, non-zero integer that should be unique within an AS. The single-positive annotation remains valid for this uniqueness SHOULD: intentional shared identifiers use the documented operator opt-out, while Section 2.2's zero and internal-self rejection remains mandatory. TestRouterIDClaimConcurrentOnlyOneWins now prepares one actual Session per Peer before all sixteen validators start together. It retains exactly-one acceptance, routerIDConflictError for every loser, a recorded holder, and no neighboring-key claim. Peer.validateOpen reads the prepared AS identity and routerIDClaims.claim serializes the check and insertion under one leaf mutex. Session-owned claim bookkeeping preserves, rather than relaxes, cross-Peer uniqueness. TestRFC6286LocalIdentifierUniqueWithinItsAS separately sends the local identifier from an internal peer and requires ErrBadBGPIdentifier, exact NOTIFICATION 2/3 and no OpenConfirm. Open.ValidateBGPIdentifier still tests internal plus equal local identifier. These assertions cover the remote-peer and local-speaker uniqueness cases; permitting every duplicate or accepting the internal self identifier violates an exact assertion. No broader startup or per-peer identifier-configuration conformance is credited by this row.
